Get interjections and their targets

Source: R/query-views.R
get_interjections.Rd

Reads the v_interjection_target view: one row per interjection, with the turn it interrupted. The view holds only two action ids; this function joins them back to actions, sittings and members to add the sitting, the chamber and both members.

Usage

get_interjections(
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  chamber = NULL,
  chamber_venue = NULL,
  interjector = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  columns = NULL,
  collect = TRUE,
  limit = NULL
)

Arguments

from, to

Sitting-date bounds, inclusive: a year (covering the whole year), a Date, or a "YYYY-MM-DD" string. NULL leaves that end open.

chamber

"house" and/or "senate", in any case.

chamber_venue

Filter on the interjection's chamber_venue: a vector of values or in_range().

interjector, target

Character vector of member PHIDs (the interjecting member, or the member interrupted). A PHID that matches no member is an error; use find_member() to look one up.

columns

Character vector of columns to return; NULL returns all.

collect

If TRUE (the default), return a tibble; if FALSE, a lazy table for further dplyr work.

limit

Maximum number of rows to return, or NULL for no limit.

Value

A tibble with one row per interjection and columns interjection_action_id, target_action_id, sitting_id, date, chamber, chamber_venue, interjector_PHID, interjector_name, target_PHID, target_name and interjection_type (the interjection's action_type: "speech" or "unresolved_interjection"). Zero rows if nothing matches; a lazy table if collect = FALSE.

Details

Every interjection in the view is returned, including those with no known interjector or no target:

  • interjector_PHID (and so interjector_name) is NA for presiding-officer interjections (resolution = "sentinel" in actions) and for unresolved interjections.

  • target_action_id (and so target_PHID and target_name) is NA when no substantive turn precedes the interjection in its subdebate.

The target is the first action of the contiguous substantive turn the interjection falls in: consecutive non-interjection actions by the same member count as one turn. Names are each member's current members.DisplayName, not their name at the time. Stored values are returned unchanged.

See also

get_sitting_timeline(), in_range()

Examples

db_connect(sample = TRUE)
get_interjections(from = 2019, to = 2019)
#> # A tibble: 34 × 11
#>    interjection_action_id target_action_id       sitting_id   date       chamber
#>    <chr>                  <chr>                  <chr>        <date>     <chr>  
#>  1 senate_2019-11-26_R108 senate_2019-11-26_R107 senate_2019… 2019-11-26 senate 
#>  2 senate_2019-11-26_R109 senate_2019-11-26_R107 senate_2019… 2019-11-26 senate 
#>  3 senate_2019-11-26_R120 senate_2019-11-26_R119 senate_2019… 2019-11-26 senate 
#>  4 senate_2019-11-26_R133 senate_2019-11-26_R132 senate_2019… 2019-11-26 senate 
#>  5 senate_2019-11-26_R134 senate_2019-11-26_R132 senate_2019… 2019-11-26 senate 
#>  6 senate_2019-11-26_R135 senate_2019-11-26_R132 senate_2019… 2019-11-26 senate 
#>  7 senate_2019-11-26_R136 senate_2019-11-26_R132 senate_2019… 2019-11-26 senate 
#>  8 senate_2019-11-26_R137 senate_2019-11-26_R132 senate_2019… 2019-11-26 senate 
#>  9 senate_2019-11-26_R149 senate_2019-11-26_R148 senate_2019… 2019-11-26 senate 
#> 10 senate_2019-11-26_R179 senate_2019-11-26_R178 senate_2019… 2019-11-26 senate 
#> # ℹ 24 more rows
#> # ℹ 6 more variables: chamber_venue <int>, interjector_PHID <chr>,
#> #   interjector_name <chr>, target_PHID <chr>, target_name <chr>,
#> #   interjection_type <chr>
get_interjections(chamber = "Senate", columns = c("interjector_name", "target_name"))
